decisions.executionNote: Begin a gentle elbow-up left approach to the standing cola bottle, keeping the right arm parked and both grippers open.
Translate the left open gripper toward the cola body above the lying white bottle, preserving wrist orientation.
Align the left fingers laterally with cola and advance slowly to surround its mid-body; grasp depth remains visually uncertain.
Close on the centered cola body after a small forward adjustment, then test retention with a short vertical lift.
Cola appears retained during the test lift; raise it and carry left toward the bin with a continuously closed grasp.
Carry the visibly retained cola farther left above the dustbin opening, keeping clearance and the same continuous arm configuration.
Move the cola safely inside the bin rim before opening the left gripper to drop it; observe its fall next.
Retract from the released cola and begin an elevated approach to the lying white bottle, gradually pitching the left gripper downward.
Replan from the interrupted pose with smaller translation and pitch increments while moving toward the white bottle.
Approach above the lying white bottle while pitching toward an overhead grasp; cola is no longer on the table.
Center the left wrist over the white bottle and complete a near-vertical approach, leaving the fingers open for visual alignment.
Lower the open fingers around the white bottle body, close fully, and test retention with a small upward lift.
Lift the white bottle clear and begin carrying left. Start a gentle right-side approach toward the standing green bottle without crossing the arms.
White bottle remained on the table: reopen and recenter the overhead grasp farther right over its body. Continue the right open-gripper approach to green.
Correct left grasp laterally and descend to the white bottle's body before closing; align the right hand at the green bottle's mid-height.
Test the corrected white grasp with a lift. Back the right fingers away from the displaced green bottle before recentering to avoid further lateral pushing.
White again stayed on the table. Reopen, shift to its updated center, and lower the overhead grip more deeply around the body; keep the right arm stationary.
Set the fingers slightly deeper around the centered white bottle, close fully, pause, and make a short retention-test lift.
Lift with the left grip fully closed to verify the deeper grasp retains the white bottle before transporting it.
White now follows the lifted gripper. Carry it left with extra height, gradually relaxing the downward pitch while retaining the bottle.
Continue carrying the retained white bottle over the dustbin interior, keeping it elevated and closed until safely beyond the rim.
Open the left gripper over the bin to release white. Begin elevating and pitching the right gripper for an overhead approach to the lying pink bottle.
The previous command was rejected without release. Open left over the bin now and use much smaller right increments to preserve joint continuity.
White is visibly falling into the bin. Reposition the open left hand toward the green bottle now near center while carefully advancing the right hand toward pink.
Approach above the remaining lying bottles with open hands, rotating the left jaws across green's long axis and raising the right wrist for an overhead pink grasp.
Continue overhead alignment, keeping the left hand to the left of center for green and right hand above pink; rotate jaws perpendicular to each bottle.
Replan with small left increments after the continuity rejection, lowering over green's left-side neck while completing the right overhead orientation.
Nudge the left fingers forward around green's neck and close. Lower and finish aligning the right open hand over pink's body.
Test green's neck grasp with a straight lift. Move the right fingers slightly forward and deeper around pink, then close for a retention check.
Neither bottle visibly followed the grips. Reopen, recenter over the displaced bodies, and lower more deeply, keeping the left wrist on its own side.
Make small image-guided lateral corrections to center the remaining bottles between the jaws, then close both and begin a short lift test.
Recover left reach margin by withdrawing slightly and tilting the fingers forward toward green. Recenter the right overhead hand over pink's visibly displaced body.
Retry the rejected recovery with half-sized left increments while maintaining the right-hand image-guided alignment.
Raise to clear the bottles before moving farther forward. Angle the left approach forward to reduce reach demand and align the right over the pink body.
Use smaller forward-tilted approaches instead of extending farther: left toward green's neck and right toward pink's body, with open fingers and continuous elbows.
Advance the finger centers forward with gradual wrist tilt and small translations; wrist views still show both bottles offset toward the forward side of the jaws.
Set both fingers deeper around the visible bottle bodies, close fully, and begin a short lift test without lateral transport.
Test the right grip with a vertical lift. Green remains beside the left jaws, so reopen and angle the fingertips toward its neck while keeping the left wrist left of center.
Both bottles remain on the table. Reopen and correct the grasp centers: left fingertips slightly forward and right, right wrist farther right and lower around pink.
Close the now-centered left grip and lower the right fingers slightly before closing; pause and lift gently to test both grasps visually.
Test right retention with a straight lift. Left grip appears empty; reopen and redirect toward green's body using a small backward correction and wrist yaw.
Neither grasp retained a bottle. Reopen, center the right hand farther left over pink and descend, while bringing the left fingers forward and down around green.
Set the aligned fingers slightly deeper, close both grippers, and test with a short vertical lift before any transport.
The fingers appear to close above the bottles. Reopen and descend gradually to enclose the bodies, correcting the right grip toward pink's center.
Lift clear to correct gripper roll: the jaws are tilted into the tabletop rather than closing horizontally around the lying bottles.
Complete jaw-roll corrections at clearance height and position over the updated bottle locations, keeping the left approach angled from its own workspace.
Replan with small retreating left increments to regain reach margin while correcting the side approach; finish right alignment over pink with horizontal closing jaws.
Lower the right hand directly around pink with a corrected vertical approach and level jaw axis; hold left position while finishing its roll correction.
Correct the forward offset seen in both wrist views before closing; move right away from contact on pink's near edge and left toward green with small increments.
After the reach guard, use a right-side angled approach while retreating the wrist forward reach; keep the closing axis level and lower left in smaller increments.
Use small lateral corrections along the jaw-opening direction. Close right around pink without pushing farther down; advance left toward green at reduced speed.
Retreat the left wrist to restore extension margin after IK rejection. Close the right grip at its current alignment and make a small retention-test lift.
Use half-sized left recovery increments following the zero-step rejection; close and test the right grip without lateral transport.
Hold the left arm stationary after repeated continuity rejections; finish closing and gently lift the right grip to determine whether pink is retained.
Pink remains on the table. Reopen and lower the right grasp substantially toward its body, while withdrawing the left wrist in very small increments to recover reach margin.
Correct the rejected tensor without compensating motion. Close the deeper right grasp and test its lift while withdrawing left in small increments.
Recenter from the head view using the visible finger midpoint, not the wrist: right toward pink's left/near side, left fingertips forward and right toward green.
Replan the zero-step rejection with smaller initial right increments, keeping both hands open while correcting their finger-center alignment.
Make small finger-centered corrections around both bottles, retaining reach margin by tilting the left approach rather than extending its wrist farther forward.
Close after a small final alignment correction, pause, and perform a short vertical retention test without lateral carrying.
Reset to a clean overhead right grasp centered on pink with jaws across its long axis. Withdraw the left hand to avoid disturbing green while focusing on one bottle.
Use smaller right alignment increments after the continuity interruption and lower slightly rather than extending upward; left stays clear.
Keep the corrected jaw orientation fixed and shift right laterally toward pink's body, retreating slightly in forward reach rather than forcing the blocked descent.
Apply a small final right-hand centering correction, close on pink with the jaws across its body, and test with a short lift.
Verify pink retention with a closed-gripper lift and slight retreat, keeping the left hand stationary and avoiding additional far-reach extension.
Pink was not retained. Reopen and approach its updated center from above, keeping the jaw orientation fixed and lowering toward the bottle rather than closing high.
Make a small final correction across the jaw opening, lower to enclose pink's body, close fully, and test with a short lift.
Test the apparently enclosed pink bottle by lifting and retreating with a fully closed right grip; move the left hand back to clear a future handover.
Pink appears to follow the right gripper. Carry it toward a central handover while orienting the left hand to receive from its own side, keeping the right grasp closed.
Bring the retained pink bottle to the center, approaching its free neck with the left open gripper while each wrist stays in its own workspace.
Pink is hanging from the right grip. Raise it slightly and bring it to the central boundary while the left hand approaches its lower body without crossing the wrists.
Hold the right bottle steady while moving the left open fingers farther around its lower body; slightly unwind the left wrist to maintain joint-limit margin.
Advance the left fingers around pink's lower body and close for the handover, while the right grip continues supporting the bottle.
Maintain the left body grasp, release the supporting right grip, and separate gently to verify that pink has transferred to the left hand.
The left grip appears above pink rather than retaining it. Reopen and lower around its body while moving the released right hand clear.
Close the lowered left grip around the pink body and test a small lift, keeping the right hand open and retreating clear of the transfer area.
The left grip did not retain pink. Clear the left hand and reapproach pink from above with the right jaws across its length for a better-supported transfer.
Separate the hands to remove interference. Correct the right wrist to a vertical approach with level jaws before descending around pink.
Lower the vertically aligned right fingers around pink's mid-body with a small centering correction, keeping the left hand clear.
Set the right fingers slightly deeper around the centered pink bottle, close fully, and verify retention with a vertical lift.
Lift the retained pink bottle to a stable handover height and position the left open hand beside its exposed lower body, keeping the supporting right grip closed.
